turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she was being foolish, that she would not leave them, and that he would care for her until the end of his days

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid softly asked O-lan if there was anything she could do to make her more comfortable.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the maid that she was comfortable, but that she needed her to help with the preparations for the eldest son's wedding, as she could not do much herself anymore

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid asked O-lan if there was anything specific she needed to start with, and if there were any plans for the wedding preparations.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the maid that she wanted to speak with the eldest son, and for him to come to the room immediately, so that she could discuss the wedding preparations with him.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that he would speak with the maid immediately to make the necessary arrangements for the wedding, and that he would bring a list of potential brides for her to review.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she would see to the arrangements immediately, and asked which of the potential brides her husband's mother would like her to bring forward first.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told the maid to bring forward the one from the north, the daughter of the rich farmer, for she had a kind face and a gentle manner.

turns.speaker: the maid
turns.text: The maid told O-lan that she had sent for the daughter of the rich farmer, but that it would be a few days before she could arrive, as the journey from the north would be long and difficult.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan's eyes moved to the eldest son, her face a picture of determination.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his mother that everything would be all right, that he would take care of her and the family, and that he would marry soon as she wished.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked, her voice barely above a whisper, if her son would really marry soon, as she had wished, and take care of his family as she had taught him.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told his wife, O-lan, that he had already spoken to the matchmaker, and a suitable bride had been found for their son.

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son told his parents that he was eager to meet the new bride and start his new life, reassuring them that he was ready for the responsibilities that came with marriage.

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was glad their son was eager to meet the new bride, but she must first see that the girl was properly cared for and settled in their household.

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would take care of the new bride and ensure she was properly cared for, and that O-lan need not worry about it, she must rest and recover

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan looked at Wang Lung, her eyes filled with a deep sadness, and told him that she could not rest and recover while her son remained unmarried

turns.speaker: Wang Lung
turns.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that he would make arrangements for their son's marriage as soon as possible, but she must focus on her own recovery

turns.speaker: O-lan
turns.text: O-lan asked Wang Lung when he would begin making arrangements for their son's marriage, her eyes fixed on him with a determined glint

turns.speaker: the eldest son
turns.text: The eldest son smiled reassuringly and told his mother that he would begin making arrangements for his marriage as soon as she gave the nod, his eyes locked on hers with a look of eagerness.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that there was another thing she had to attend to before she could die.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung insisted that O-lan should not speak of dying and that it would please him if she did not.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan replied that she had to die, for she felt it in her vitals waiting, but she would not die before her eldest son came home and before he wedded this good maid who was her daughter-in-law, and well she served O-lan, holding the hot water basin steadily and knowing when to bathe O-lan's face when she sweated in pain. Now O-lan wanted her son to come home, because she had to die, and she wanted him to wed this maid first, so that she might die easily, knowing that her grandson was stirred into life and a great-grandson for the old one.

opening.speaker: Wang Lung
opening.text: Wang Lung told O-lan that she looked twice as well as they had said and years away from death.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan declared that she would see Wang Lung wedded and then she must die.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan instructed Wang Lung to sit there and drink the wine and eat the rice of his marriage, for she would see it all and this would be his bed of marriage since she was soon to be finished with it and carried away.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan asked if everyone had wine, if the sweet rice dish in the middle of the feast was very hot, if they had put full measure of lard and sugar into it, and if the eight fruits were present.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan told Wang Lung that she was now content and that this thing in her may do as it would. She instructed her son to look to his father and his grandfather, and her daughter to look to her husband and his father and his grandfather and the poor fool in the court, there she was. And she told Wang Lung that he had no duty to any other.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan said that, even if she was ugly, she had borne a son; although she was but a slave, there was a son in her house.

opening.speaker: O-lan
opening.text: O-lan insisted that no one else could feed Wang Lung's son and care for him as she did. She told Wang Lung that beauty would not bear a man sons.
